searchText: I'm extremely loath to tell people to write code like this <@!425572898787426305> <@!291925846556540928>: ```typescript try { eth_getBlockByNumber('finalized') // TODO: PoS finalized-based decision making } catch (error) { if (error.message === NO_FINALIZED_BLOCK_YET_MESSAGE) { // TODO: PoW confirmation-based decision making } } ``` There are books (probably) written on why this is ~~bad~~ terrible code. I agree. This is an anti pattern If your basis on this being terrible is the try/catch I don't see why that's needed: ``` response = eth_getBlockByNumber('finalized') if response.error && response.error.message == NO_FINALIZED_BLOCK_YET_MESSAGE { // POW } else { // POS } ``` But maybe you meant having to check the blockbynumber result at all? That assumes that you don't have some higher level architecture for dealing with errors (which feels like ae bad design in the first place).
